meanings: noun: result; effect; what happens because of an event
examples: If you hurt the people around you, there will be unwanted consequences.

meanings: noun: an area of land
examples: Although most of the Japanese exchange students come from Osaka, in the south, Akiko comes from Sapporo, in the northern region of Japan.

meanings: adjective: very important, or large in size
examples: The exam score is a major part of the final class grade.

meanings: verb: to help or aid
examples: The box was too big to carry, so John asked the store manager to assist him.

meanings: verb: to look at; to think about; to give attention to
noun: the center of attention; the most important part
examples: I could not focus on my homework in the library because someone was playing music very loudly.
The focus of Justin's essay was not clear to the professor, so he received a low grade.

meanings: adjective: happening before the one happening now (of a thing, event, or date)
examples: Soojin thought her science class was really hard after studying only literature in the previous year.

meanings: verb: to make as big as possible; to use or do as completely as possible
examples: In order to maximize the number of people that can fit on the plane, the airline took out the restrooms.

meanings: verb: to say which one or clearly point to which one
examples: The king told the hero that he could marry one of the princesses but did not specify which one.

meanings: verb: to form an idea of the amount, number, or value of something
examples: Students are evaluated by their grades on tests, homework, essays, and in-class interaction.

meanings: noun: the state of touching
noun: having possible or normal communication
verb: communicating (as by email or phone especially) to give or get specific information
examples: An electrical wire in contact with a pool of water can be extremely dangerous.
Liam is still in contact with many of his high-school teachers, surprisingly.
The woman at the help desk told me to contact the student affairs office if I want to change rooms.

meanings: adjective: closely connected to the topic and therefore important
examples: I think Professor McGarry can give you some relevant books to help you write that essay.

meanings: verb: to communicate without saying specifically; to lead to (a conclusion)
examples: The president implied that he would not support the new law against selling tobacco, but he didn't say it clearly.

meanings: adjective: not very important; small in size
examples: The old actress was sad she had only a minor role in the new movie.

meanings: verb: to say no to something offered; to refuse or decline
examples: After applying to ten schools, Lucas was rejected by nine of them.

meanings: adjective: of the mind
examples: Many mental problems are still not well understood. We often don't know what causes them nor how to stop them from happening.

meanings: verb: to depend on; to need in order to continue well
examples: In many countries, children rely on their parents for food, money, and housing until they are over 20 years old.

meanings: verb: to pass from one person or thing to another
examples: Sally transferred all of her money from American National Bank when she heard they were closing.

meanings: noun: a range or amount of time
examples: Computer technology changed a lot in the period between 1980 and 2000.

meanings: verb: to be in or on a space; to fill a space
examples: The dentist's office occupied the entire fourth floor of the building.

meanings: noun: a plan of action to reach a desired goal
examples: The debate team spent the evening discussing their strategy for defeating the other team

meanings: adjective: easily understood or seen
examples: The results of the election were so obvious that the loser admitted defeat before voting was finished.

meanings: noun: an observation, note, or response
verb: to say a short response or opinion about a given topic
examples: The professor was angry about the negative comments made about his teaching style.
A smart politician, the prime minister refused to comment on the criticisms of her newest budget plan.

meanings: noun: the ability to go into (when somebody or something must allow you to enter)
verb: to go into; to reach (when able to or allowed to enter)
examples: Only students have access to the university library.
There is a large amount of oil under the ice, but we can't access it.

meanings: verb: to make larger; to give more detail on a subject
examples: Blowing air into a balloon will cause it to expand, but if you blow too much air, it will explode!

meanings: noun: one of a number of pieces which come together to create a whole
examples: Every ant's body has three sections: a head, a thorax (where the legs are), and an abdomen (the back).

meanings: noun: first in importance
examples: The primary cause of unhappiness is not about money—it is bad health.

meanings: adjective: able to be reached, used, or bought
examples: The advisor was not available to meet all day Monday, so the student had to come back on Tuesday.

meanings: noun: the situation; facts or environment around an event
examples: My professor only gives extra time to finish essays under special circumstances. Normally it's not allowed.

meanings: verb: to answer
verb: to react
examples: Waiters who respond to customers' questions with a smile generally get more money.
If you scare a turtle, it will respond by hiding in its shell.

meanings: noun: a name or phrase given to a group of things to identify them (often negative)
verb: to give a label to something
examples: The meaning of the label "punk" has changed greatly in the last 30 years.
Children are often unkind and label others who look different as outsiders.

meanings: verb: to get (especially when you will continue to get more)
examples: Janice isn't a doctor yet, but from her studies she is slowly acquiring the knowledge and skills she'll need.

meanings: noun: where something comes from
examples: Do not trust books that give information without listed sources. The facts could be false.

meanings: verb: to respond; to act in answer to
examples: Mothers react quickly to their babies' cries, even in the middle of the night.

meanings: adjective: single or separated; only one of
examples: Joan was surprised that the ten books she ordered from the internet came together, but in individual boxes.

meanings: verb: to happen
examples: The sinking of the Titanic occurred on the night of April 14, 1912.

meanings: noun: something difficult
verb: to suggest a fight or argument; to disagree or try to fight somebody
verb: to say something isn't true
examples: New medicines face many challenges before they can be put in stores.
In order to get the attention of females, males of many animal species will challenge each other in different ways.
Einstein's writings challenged many ideas of the time.

meanings: verb: to change; to make different; to have an effect
examples: Which language we speak affects how we think about the world.

meanings: verb: to join or take part (in an activity)
examples: The teacher was surprised when every student participated in the math game.

meanings: verb: to agree; to decide; to solve a problem or argument
examples: Even after meeting for hours, the government leaders still could not resolve their argument over new taxes.

meanings: verb: to organize and manage (an event that takes careful planning and control)
examples: My research team is conducting a study on how the internet is changing dating in five countries.

meanings: noun: some saved material that can be used for a purpose (especially money, oil, or books)
examples: Many of the richest countries have surprisingly few natural resources and must buy oil from other countries.
Use the library during your studies; it's full of great resources.

meanings: adjective: of the body (not the mind)
adjective: concrete (something real that you can touch or feel)
examples: Cleaning up the campus garden was tiring, physical work.
Katerina doesn't like paying for music without a physical copy, such as a CD.

meanings: adjective: clearly seen or understood; obvious
examples: Dogs' feelings are usually evident in their actions.

meanings: noun: A place to find valuable information including IELTS study tips. Learn more at magoosh.com/ielts.
verb: to find or search for more information about something
noun: information collected about something (usually academic)
examples: After growing up on an island, Malika hoped to research ocean temperatures in graduate school.
Dr. Stanislaus was famous for his research on changes in health education over the past 100 years.

meanings: verb: to continue
verb: to keep alive; to keep in good state or condition
verb: to continue to say although people disagree
examples: China has maintained a friendship with the U.S., although the two countries often have different needs and ideas.
These roads are so badly maintained that they're difficult to drive on.
Until his death, Christopher Columbus maintained that he had sailed to Asia, not America.

meanings: adjective: complicated; having many different parts and difficult to understand
examples: The science behind the atomic bomb used in World War II was highly complex at the time, but it is simple compared to today's nuclear science.

meanings: verb: to finally do something you have been trying hard to do
examples: The best students know that to achieve good grades, they have to study every day.

meanings: verb: to build
examples: The land flooded every year, so it was unsafe to construct buildings on it.

meanings: noun: the way a group of people living in one area normally acts, including arts, style, food, and how people talk to and act with each other
examples: When living in another country, it can be very difficult to become comfortable in the new culture.

meanings: verb: to take away or take out
examples: The grocery store removed all of the milk after the government said it was unsafe to drink.
